root_cause.text: In the spi-nor debugfs code, spi_nor_params_show() incorrectly passed sizeof(snor_f_names) for an array-of-pointers length to spi_nor_print_flags(), so the bounds check used byte size instead of element count and allowed out-of-bounds reads from the names array.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `spi_nor_print_flags(s, nor->flags, snor_f_names, sizeof(snor_f_names));` to use `ARRAY_SIZE(snor_f_names)`, and the CVE/commit explicitly states that `sizeof()` on the pointer array made `names_len` larger than the real element count, causing out-of-bounds access in `spi_nor_print_flags()`.

bic_trace_step.reason: The relevant logic is fully visible in this snippet. In `spi_nor_params_show()`, the call `spi_nor_print_flags(s, nor->flags, snor_f_names, sizeof(snor_f_names));` passes `sizeof(snor_f_names)` as `names_len`. But `snor_f_names` is declared as `static const char *const snor_f_names[]`, so `sizeof(snor_f_names)` is the array size in bytes, not the number of elements. In `spi_nor_print_flags()`, the bounds check is `if (i < names_len && names[i])`, which assumes `names_len` is an element count. Because `names_len` is too large on pointer arrays, the code can read past the end of `names[]` via `names[i]` for set bits beyond the real element count. Therefore the vulnerable construct is present, and the fix (using the element count, e.g. `ARRAY_SIZE(snor_f_names)`) is not present.
